A1.justification: Both 12-page PDFs describe the same PrefixKV work. Text, equations, figures, tables, and references support reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix or supplement, although both mention supplementary examples.

before.justification: v1 reports original PrefixKV benchmark evaluations, inference-time measurements, ablations, and generation examples in Section 4 and Tables 1–9.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark evaluations, inference-time measurements, ablations, and generation examples in Section 4 and Tables 1–9.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same attention-based importance ranking, binary search for global prefix allocation, offline estimation, and decoding-time eviction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LLaVA-Description and MM-Vet datasets and retain the same instruction-following tasks and test scenarios. No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain identical, including Local (StreamingLLM), H2O, Elastic Cache, uncompressed models, and the baseline/PyramidKV comparison in Table 3.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical model configurations, instruction-tuning exclusions, PPL/ROUGE metrics, decoding temperatures, compression budgets, sample counts, and inference-timing procedures.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the same analyses of layer allocation, offline versus online estimation, calibration sample count, eviction versus merging, feature disturbance, and chat generation.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the plots based on 100 random samples in Figures 4–5. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-estimation, or significance-testing information changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–9 and the empirical plots retain identical results. For example, Table 1 reports 3.69 PPL and 0.51 ROUGE for PrefixKV with LLaVA-1.5-7B at a 20% compression budget in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(4), binary-search reasoning, and merging formulas in Section 4.3 are unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about adaptive prefix allocation, contextual-information retention, generation quality, and inference efficiency, including the stated 1.8× speedup.

C2.justification: Interpretations of layer heterogeneity, offline estimation, merging interference, and the W-shaped cache allocation remain identical. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: The code-access link and implementation disclosures remain identical, including 10 offline calibration samples, decoding rules, and NVIDIA A100 timing hardware.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations throughout the paper, and all 80 reference entries are unchanged. The positioning relative to previous KV-cache compression research is identical.

P1.justification: v3 adds Jiaxin Li to the author list and updates the arXiv version/date stamp from v1 dated 4 December 2024 to v3 dated 14 July 2025. Body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5, Tables 1–9, and Algorithm 1 retain identical formatting, captions, and placement. The page and column organization is unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revisions are confined to the author list and version/date stamp. The method, experimental evidence, analyses, technical disclosures, and exposition remain unchanged, producing no meaningful net difference in paper quality.
